SymbolicEssence.ArchetypalFunction: To embody sleep, rest, and the threshold between waking and dreaming; to provide respite and regeneration.
SymbolicEssence.SymbolicCore: The gentle darkness of sleep, brother to death, father of dreams.

MythicAppearances: Father of Morpheus and dream gods
CulturalContext.ReligiousOrRitualUse: Invoked for sleep and rest; associated with healing temples of Asclepius; offerings of poppies and milk.
CulturalContext.HistoricalEvolution: Ancient sleep deity; twin of Thanatos; dwelling in underworld near Lethe; merged with Roman Somnus.

SymbolicRepresentation.ImageryNotes: Depicted as gentle winged youth, sometimes winged at temples; touching mortals with magic wand or pouring from horn; surrounded by poppies.
SymbolicRepresentation.PoeticInvocation: Sweet Hypnos, gentle brother, who brings rest to gods and mortals alike.
SymbolicRepresentation.DreamForm: Soft wings brushing your eyelids as consciousness gently fades into renewal

MetaIntegration.RitualFunction: Invoked for restful sleep, healing dreams, and regeneration of body and spirit.
AIPromptSeeds: The gentle god who brings rest even to the king of gods.
Sleep personified, the necessary darkness that renews all things.
NarrativeHooks: The character who cannot sleep or rest
The threshold between waking and dreaming
